subject: Post-call: Scaling KV cache, SLO targets, and deployment topology — Next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neil <liam.oneil@ravenmed.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-21T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: Scaling KV cache, SLO targets, and deployment topology — Next steps

Hi Liam — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from Redwood and the concrete next steps so we stay aligned.

High-level goals you called out
- Primary: 95th %-tile tail latency below 350ms for user-facing generation flows at typical prompt sizes (<= 256 tokens).
- Secondary: sustained throughput of 800–1,000 requests/sec for background summarization jobs (batch windows off-peak).
- Data controls: all inference logs retained for 30 days and routed to RavenMed's SIEM.

Key pain points you shared
- Large spike variance when clinical prompts include long patient histories (~800–1,200 tokens).
- Cold-start latency on infrequent model variants when KV cache is expired.
- Cost sensitivity for experimental model variants — need clear perf vs cost tradeoffs.

Technical alignment (high level)
- Model profile: recommendation is a 3-tier approach — base generation variant (fp16 + 8-bit quant for cost), a high-accuracy variant (fp16 full), and a constrained low-latency variant with prefix-KV pinning.
- KV cache: automatic prefix caching for stable sessions + optional sticky routing to keep KV warm for 95th %-tile critical flows. This should reduce repeated attention recomputation for long-context prompts.
- SLO targets we propose to validate in a PoC:
  * P50 end-to-end: < 120ms (short prompts <= 64 tokens)
  * P95 end-to-end: < 350ms (typical prompts <= 256 tokens)
  * Sustained throughput test: 1,000 rps for background batches over 15-minute window with 99% request success

Requested items from RavenMed to scope PoC
1) Sample traffic profile (top 5000 requests by frequency) and 20 representative long-context prompts.
2) Expected concurrency during peak hour and preferred test region (you mentioned us-west2).
3) Compliance checklist items for SIEM integration and retention (we'll need the contact for your security/ops team).

Next steps (timeline)
- By Thu (2027-11-25): RavenMed shares sample traffic + security contact.
- Week of 2027-11-29: Redwood runs a 2-day profiling run in us-west2 and shares a short perf report.
- Week of 2027-12-06: Joint deep-dive (1hr) to review PoC results and finalize mutual action plan.

Attachments: redwood_kv_cache_whitepaper.pdf (overview), mutual_action_plan_ravenmed.xlsx (MVP checklist)

Thanks — I looped Sean on the cloud/ops items and Marissa on contract/timing.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Scaling KV cache, SLO targets, and deployment topology — Next steps

Thanks Mina — this is exactly what we needed, nice summary. A few quick notes from RavenMed:

- We can provide the top traffic slice and 20 long-context examples by end-of-day Thursday. Ops will share the SIEM contact (security@ravenmed.com).
- For the PoC, us-west2 is correct. We also want to test a DR path in us-east1 if possible (low-effort replication).
- Can you confirm whether the KV warm-up sticky routing impacts multi-tenant isolation for our Dedicated pool? We need isolation guarantees for PHI workloads.

Also: we want a lightweight canary plan for switching between the ‘cost’ and ‘accuracy’ variants without user impact — can your team draft one?

Appreciate it — Liam
Liam O'Neil
Head of Platform, RavenMed Health
liam.oneil@ravenmed.com

Liam — quick technical clarifications from infra so we can scope the PoC properly: 

1) Isolation: for Dedicated pools we can provide network / compute isolation and KMS-backed key separation. KV caching is local to the serving cluster and does not expose cross-tenant state. We'll include a short architecture diagram in the perf report.

2) Canary plan sketch (for your ops/PM):
  - Ramp traffic to cost-variant 10% at T+0, monitor P95 and error rate for 30 minutes.
  - If P95 increases > 20% or error rate > 0.5% revert to accuracy variant.
  - If stable for 3 consecutive windows, continue 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 hours.

3) Throughput tests: we'll run two modes — steady stream at target QPS and elevated burst tests (to validate autoscaling). We need your preferred test accounts to avoid cross-mixing with prod data.

4) Model variants: please confirm the baseline model family you want profiled (your notes said rg-34b and rg-7b equivalents). If you require a proprietary model, we'll need the model artifact and an NDA addendum.

I'll attach the early test matrix and a short ops checklist to the perf report.

-Sean
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
